section_summary.extract_value: This section describes use of a 6-item subscale from the Interest in Cosmetic Surgery Scale (Markey & Markey, 2009) to assess interest in low-cost, low-invasiveness cosmetic procedures; responses ranged 1–5 and item averages formed the subscale total. Internal consistency was reported (women α = .75, men α = .72) and the sample size is noted as N = 261; a table/note indicates women's correlations are above the diagonal and men's are below.
section_summary.evidence_source: A subscale from the Interest in Cosmetic Surgery Scale (Markey & Markey, 2009) was used to assess interest in cosmetic enhancements.... Internal consistency reliability scores were adequate (women ˛= .75, men ˛= .72). Note: N = 261. Women's correlations are above the diagonal and men's are below.

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes a 6-item subscale from the Interest in Cosmetic Surgery Scale assessing interest in low-cost, low-invasiveness cosmetic procedures (response 1–5); higher scores indicate greater interest, with internal consistency α = .75 for women and .72 for men. Table 1 (N = 261) provides means, SDs, and correlations for study variables; the table note states that women’s correlations are above the diagonal and men’s are below.
section_summary.evidence_source: Section text: 'A subscale from the Interest in Cosmetic Surgery Scale (Markey & Markey, 2009) ... The average of the items was used for the subscale total. Higher scores indicate greater interest in cosmetic enhancements. Internal consistency reliability scores were adequate (women ˛= .75, men ˛= .72).' Table 1 note: 'Note: N = 261. Women\'s correlations are above the diagonal and men\'s are below.'
